entry.code_revision: THE AUTHOR'S OWN SERVER, run unmodified: aminry/decisio at 4f849ff2dbae10a53026e382ce3dd60b95780594 (one commit after tag v0.32.0 e7e8937f35b0611d327295563b0cffbeb8bafdc3; the commit changes README.md only, so every src/ file equals the tag; package decisio 0.32.0), installed on the pod with the author's own 'uv sync --extra serve --frozen' from the repository's uv.lock (sha256 d82e40ba4b3693a17e7cd85f17604d1f818fae6dad431293e3b4541932bbbbe3) with credentials absent, before any sealed byte; the sealed run itself had no network. Entrypoint: python -m decisio.serve.vllm_engine --base /model --max-model-len 32768 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000, every other flag at its 0.32.0 default (over-limit refuse, header-limit auto, concurrency serial, orders 1, think off, no adapters, no branch log, no task store, stock vLLM with no patches), HF offline flags set. The server's native endpoint POST /v1/systemone was used with no response shim and no launcher shim; the request path is the frozen v1.6 measurement driver with the frozen TypeSafe adapter. The only flag outside the author's defaults, --max-model-len 32768, fixes the context length: without it 0.32.0 picks an automatic length up to 65,536 that depends on the model card, which would make the refusal set card-dependent. On-pod asserts passed before any sealed input: distribution versions decisio 0.32.0, vllm 0.31.0, torch 2.13.0, transformers 5.17.0, triton 3.7.1 (tokenizers 0.23.2 in uv.lock; python 3.12); /health flavor report {name commit, served_name Decisio-12b-tuned-commit, overrides {}, pending []}; abstention_tasks {} (no task source configured, so no per-task calibration, head or abstention applies). Source review (line by line over the request path, before measurement): no branch on item text, ids, gold labels or item lists; the disclosed item-blind label-shape rules do inspect option keys/descriptions. No network, subprocess, eval or pickle on the request path; no stop condition. Model: tachara-ai/Decisio-12b-tuned-commit at 245e00dc45abad14d693b1ebae4d4c7aa9cf72f1, a MERGED BF16 checkpoint (6 safetensors shards, 23,919,548,376 shard bytes; every file hashed against the repository SHA256SUMS on the node) of google/gemma-4-12B-it at 707f0a3b8a3c7ad586ed01e27eafbad8a27dd0f7 plus a LoRA with adapter dimension 16 merged in fp32 and rounded once to bf16 (stochastic, seed 0, per the model card); on one CUDA device, no quantisation. Author code and weights were fetched by our code at the pinned revisions and ran only on a disposable rented GPU VM; the measurement kit was hash-pinned and independently reviewed before measurement, and the draw was used once for this row. Weights: 12B-class merged checkpoint, not an adapter.
entry.cost_basis: ESTIMATE (*est.), base-model market reference, explicit reference with NO base key: the frozen pricing_v15 module (sha256 aa2afcd5a58d0c4cc0e3d6867d590c70b6ac58e971410c27faf9628f97bcf8b7, re-freeze of 22 Oct 2026) has no listing for the card's base string google/gemma-4-12B-it (it is in the module's UNLISTED_BASE_MODELS set, so there is no exact rate and no floor; reference() returns nothing for it, checked on this module). The reference used is therefore google/gemma-3-12b-it USD 0.05/M input, USD 0.15/M output, the nearest publicly hosted 12B Gemma sibling, at its FULL catalog pair, the same explicit reference that the published google/gemma-4-12B-it rows cygnet, jev-omni, winnow-12b, torchcast-decision-12b and the live decisio v0.8.0 and v0.9.0 rows already carry. It is applied explicitly, as a labelled estimate; no base key is registered for it. Estimated, not charged, not a quote from the author or any host. Tokens as reported natively by the usage block of the author's server: 715,443 input and 1,485 output tokens across the 1,485 answered items (1 reported output token per answered row for the option-label readout; no generated prose). The native input unit counts header, state and question separately without the system turn or chat template. It is not a count of every token processed internally: the server can also register the state prefix through a warm-up, and that work is not added to native usage. Native input usage equals our first-party offline count exactly (0 mismatches over the answered items; our sealed-input count before the run was also 715,443). The 15 items refused HTTP 422 carry no usage and count 0 tokens, so the common 1,485-item basis (v1.6.30) has the same totals, 715,443 input and 1,485 output tokens. The zero-output convention for native-probability rows is NOT applied: the server reports a real output count of 1 per answered row (the same treatment as the live decisio rows, seb-9b-v2 and KnowLine, which price their 1 output token per row), and the full output price is used. Measured arithmetic: USD 0.024239 per 1,000 decisions on the common 1,485-item basis = 0.375248x the unchanged USD 0.06459465517241379 cap; separately USD 0.023997 per 1,000 over all 1,500 rows = 0.371495x. WITHIN COST CAP on both bases: within the automatic cost treatment; no cap exception or top-up.
entry.disclosure: FIRST MEASUREMENT of Decisio-12b-tuned-commit in this intake (our own intake). A NEW ROW, A VARIANT OF THE DECISIO FAMILY: tachara-ai/Decisio-12b-tuned-commit is a different set of weights from the live decisio-gemma-4-12b-v080 and -v090 rows, which are the stock google/gemma-4-12B-it served by decisio; none of its 6 shard LFS sha256s equals the safetensors blob of google/gemma-4-12B-it at 707f0a3b, of google/gemma-4-31B-it at 842da379, of the decisio FP8 31B repository at eaf1e4fa, or of the weights behind the live decisio rows (byte-identity evidence only, not proof of independent training). It replaces and supersedes none of the live decisio rows. The model card states that a sibling repository, Decisio-12b-tuned-calibrated, holds the same weights and differs in decision_config.json only; that sibling was not measured and nothing is inferred about it. The name is 'Jev-compatible' only: it is a Decisio model, not a Jev model. FINE-TUNE OF GEMMA 4: a LoRA merged into google/gemma-4-12B-it (see code_revision). AUTHOR'S OWN SERVER on our rented hardware, run unmodified (see code_revision) with no shim. NATIVE OUTPUTS: probabilities for choice, noul and score from the option-letter readout (vLLM max_tokens=1 for the option-label readout, softmax over the label tokens, think off; state-prefix registration can add a warm-up, excluded from native usage) at the repository's shipped per-type temperatures (yes/no 3.314, score 2.1109, choice 2-10 options 2.1317, 11-26 options 1.8766, 27-255 options 1.7181); no generated explanation. CONFIGURATION: the repository's shipped flavor 'commit', exactly as shipped; the card also names the calibrated sibling. We did not measure any other flavor or setting and infer nothing about one. JEVBENCH-AWARE DEFAULT, THE COMMIT RULE (a disclosed non-raw, item-blind output transform, treated like the DOPEST 0.801 floor): for yes/no questions, a temperature-scaled P(yes) strictly between 0.20 and 0.80 is reported at the nearer band edge, 0.80 if it is above 0.5, otherwise 0.20 (exactly 0.5 goes to 0.20). The band is exactly JevBench's own yes/no decision band: JevBench scores an answer strictly between 0.20 and 0.80 as an abstention, counted wrong, and the author's repository ships its own reading of that open-set rule (not imported by the server). On this draw the rule moved 193 of the 373 answered yes/no answers to a band edge, so the row has no yes/no abstentions; without it those answers would be scored as abstentions. It is the shipped flavor's default, measured as shipped. The argmax never changes; the Calibration axis includes the effect of this transform, and we did not measure a variant without it. LABEL-SHAPE RULES ON BY DEFAULT: hide_index_keys, describe_options and desnake_labels. The author documents hide_index_keys as motivated by the Decision Index option_N format and desnake_labels by BANKING77; they act on the shape of the labels of any request, never on item text, ids, gold labels or item lists (source review confirmed item-blind), and the answer keys are always the request's own keys. The frozen offline layout counter recorded 739 describe_options, 375 noul_as_letters and 11 hide_index_keys applications across all 1,500 draw rows, including the refused rows; desnake_labels recorded 0. Of 375 yes/no rows, 373 were answered. On the 231 public items the corresponding counts were 139 / 74 / 0 (desnake_labels 0). TRAINING DATA (author statement, not independently verified): the model card says the training data is not disclosed, that no Decision Index or JevBench evaluation items were used in training or checkpoint selection, that the data was decontaminated against both boards' public test sets, and that official training splits of some public benchmarks were used under their licences. We did not inspect the training examples or check overlap with JevBench items; contamination of the sealed draw is unchecked. The card says the temperatures were fitted by minimum log loss per question type and choice band on the plain readout; it does not identify the data of that fit. LICENCE NOTE: Apache-2.0 per the model card, LICENSE and NOTICE on the weights and per the author server licence; the base is Gemma 4 under its own terms. CONTEXT AND REFUSALS: the server refuses a row natively when even the plain layout (system turn, chat template, state, question, no header) exceeds its 32,767-token prompt limit (32,767 answered, 32,768 refused; boundary proven offline, and a row whose header alone pushes it over is answered on the plain layout instead); a refused row is never truncated. NOT ANSWERED, counted wrong: the draw's 15 standard long positions (plain-layout prompts of 76,531 to 81,726 tokens by our offline count), counted and frozen in the preregistered refusal list before launch; all returned HTTP 422 and the measured 422 set equals the preregistered set exactly (no unexpected failure; every other row HTTP 200). ANSWERED: 1,485 of 1,500. 10 s RULE: 0 decisions over 10 s, so no decision is scored wrong under the 10 s rule in the v1.7 share view (the frozen v1.6 and v1.7-off views apply no time limit); measured loopback median 0.058397072 s, interpolated p95 0.099410957 s (upper-order p95 0.099450955 s), maximum 0.167558985 s over all 1,500 requests on the recorded hardware. The v1.7 share view uses the common self-hosted latency estimate, 2 times measured p50 plus 0.15 s = 0.266794144 s; this adjustment is an assumption, not a measured hosted endpoint. USAGE: the server-native input usage (715,443 tokens) equals our first-party count exactly, 0 mismatches; output_tokens 1 per answered row natively (1,485 in total). DETERMINISM (record-only): the first 50 requests were run twice; 3 of 50 were bit-identical, 0 argmax flips, maximum probability difference 0.0195 (observed on the serial vLLM path; its cause was not isolated; a short smoke probe also varied between 0.8451876 and 0.8500589). The scored rows are the first run and stand. ATTEMPT HISTORY: one attempt, no earlier failed or discarded attempt on the sealed input; the pre-sealed smoke and gates passed before any sealed item.
